item.title: Economic Survey 2025-26 treats air pollution as a regulatory problem, not a health emergency
item.description: The Economic Survey 2025-26 frames air pollution as a regulatory issue, focusing on compliance and market tools, rather than a public-health crisis. This approach risks prioritizing economic processes over the health of those most affected by toxic air, highlighting need for a justice-first response

item.title: Budget 2026: Boost for modernisation and sustainability in Indian textile industry
item.description: The Union Budget 2026-27 introduces initiatives like the National Fibre Scheme and Tex-Eco Initiative to modernise and sustain the Indian textile industry, focusing on self-reliance, artisan support, and sustainability.

item.title: India’s Rs 20,000-crore CCUS push: What the Union Budget’s carbon capture bet really means
item.description: India's 2026-27 Budget allocates Rs 20,000 crore to boost carbon capture, storage, and utilisation in five key industrial sectors, aiming to support the country's net-zero by 2070 goal. While promising, challenges like high costs and governance issues remain critical for effective implementation.

item.title: Preventable deaths in a warming world: How politics shapes who lives & who dies
item.description: The tragic deaths of the Galvan family in Texas underscore how climate change and political neglect exacerbate vulnerabilities, particularly among the elderly and chronically ill. Addressing systemic issues is crucial to prevent future climate-related fatalities.

item.title: IPBES 12: Global biodiversity meeting begins at Manchester
item.description: The 12th IPBES Plenary in Manchester focuses on 'business and biodiversity', aiming to guide global efforts in sustainable resource use and nature protection. Delegates will review a new report on business impacts on ecosystems.
